result.benchNote:
Method: same process, cells INTERLEAVED per round (not A-block/B-block), 40 rounds, first 10 discarded as warmup, 200 reps × corpus per round, MEDIAN of 30 scored rounds, min–max spread printed, results folded into a printed sink so nothing is DCE'd. Shared corpus = 30 inputs BOTH parsers accept (benchmarking cand-O on inputs the incumbent rejects early would measure different work). Failure corpus times only inputs the incumbent rejects WITHOUT throwing. node v26.0.0 · darwin arm64 · @mkbabb/parse-that 1.0.0 · published @mkbabb/value.js 4.0.0 tarball. Re-run: `npx tsx cand-o/bench.ts`.

RESULT (stable ratios across 5 runs; absolute ns varies with machine load):
  SHARED (accepted)  cand-O parseColorNode 1.16–1.28× FASTER than published; cand-O parseColor (drop-in CssColor) 0.99–1.04× = PARITY; published = 1.00 baseline.
  FAILURE (rejected) cand-O 0.56–0.71× = SLOWER. Combinator alternation exhausts arms before failing; the incumbent bails on one regex mismatch. This is the honest cost of the design.
  Per-family (parseColor vs published): named 1.23× · oklch 1.10× · color() 1.04× · hex 0.94× · rgb legacy 0.96× · rgb modern 0.92×.

Declared asymmetries, both directions (in the bench file header, not just here): cand-O pays for backtracking (modern tried before legacy, so rgb(1,2,3) parses its first channel twice), for strictness (same-type rule, <hue> typing, `1.`-is-not-a-number, hex length set), and for a real AST with a provenance tag. The incumbent pays deepFreeze on every success, a recursive re-entry into parseCssColor for every named colour, and four String.match calls plus two hand-written split loops on the functional path.

POSTURE ON THE STANDING EVIDENCE: the prior gate's "LIVE regex measured FASTEST ~1.8×" is NOT reproduced here — but that gate measured a DIFFERENT prototype. I make no claim that the earlier measurement was wrong; I report what this grammar measures on this machine. Headline honestly stated: cand-O buys correctness at roughly break-even on accepted input and ~1.6× worse on rejected input.

FILES (all absolute under the dir):
  ast.ts (63 code lines) · spec.ts (135) · grammar.ts (258) · index.ts (133) · named-colors.ts (174, generated)
  totality.test.ts (28) · color-4.test.ts (182) · equivalence.test.ts (114) · idiom.test.ts (25) · named-colors.test.ts (6)

THE DESIGN CLAIM. The eight colour functions are ONE production, not eight. spec.ts is a channel table (percentRef / numberIsPercentage / clamp) and grammar.ts reads it; rgb() and oklch() are two ROWS. That is the structural argument against the incumbent, whose eight near-identical `if (lower === … && components.length === 3)` arms each carry their own copy of the same four mistakes. AST keeps the space the AUTHOR WROTE (`srgb` stays srgb, `xyz-d50` stays xyz-d50); the ×255 rescale and the Bradford D50→D65 adaptation live in the adapter, because a parser that silently applies a chromatic-adaptation matrix is not a parser. Nothing is discarded: currentColor, the 19 <system-color>s, var()/env() and css-color-5 relative syntax parse to ContextColor nodes; only the value.js-shaped adapter turns them into ok:false, because ParseResult<CssColor> has nowhere to put them.

IDIOM, MEASURED TWO WAYS, NOT ASSERTED. Textually on COMMENT-STRIPPED source (measuring a header that names an anti-pattern as if it were the anti-pattern is exactly GROUND-C's I-8): 0 non-null assertions by GROUND-B's own `[A-Za-z_0-9)\]]!` regex across all four sources (incumbent: 72), 0 `as any`, 0 `as unknown as`, exactly 1 `Parser.lazy`, 0 memoize, 0 `.parse(`, 0 hand-rolled cursors (no `for(let`, no `while(`, no `charCodeAt`), 13 regex terminals none of which contain `.*` or `[^)]*`. STRUCTURALLY by walking the built graph through `Parser.context`: no `opt` node is a direct child of any `all` node (a grep cannot prove this; the graph can), exactly 1 lazy node, 0 memoize/debug/recover nodes, exactly 2 dispatch nodes.

TWO PRIMITIVES THE LIBRARY LACKS, built without touching `new Parser(...)`: `succeed(v) = string("").map(() => v)` (startsWith("") is true even past EOF, so it is safe zero-width) and `never = regex(/(?!)/)`. They let the 169-keyword table and the 9-colourspace table be PRECOMPUTED parser tables resolved by `chain` — chain used for exactly what chain is for, a value-dependent continuation, with zero per-parse allocation and no dead defensive branch (the unknown-ident arm is live and reachable).

A REAL BUG CLASS CLOSED: both lookup tables are NULL-PROTOTYPE. A `Record<string, …>` built from an object literal answers `constructor`, so `color(constructor 0 0 0)` would have parsed. Asserted, plus `__proto__`/`toString`/`hasOwnProperty`/`valueOf`/`prototype`.

A DEFECT I FOUND IN MY OWN SPEC AND FIXED BEFORE WRITING THE CORPUS: css-color-4 §8.2/§8.3 make `hsl(120 50 50)` EXACTLY `hsl(120 50% 50%)`. My first cut carried `numberScale: 0.01` — but `n * 0.01 !== n / 100` for 114 of the 1001 values 0, 0.1 … 100, so the two spellings would have disagreed in the last ulp. Replaced with a `numberIsPercentage` flag that reuses the percentage expression verbatim; pinned by a bit-equality test over 6 values. The percentage arithmetic is written `(value * ref) / 100` — value.js's exact association — so agreement with the incumbent is bit-for-bit, not merely close.

TOTALITY — 28 tests. R1 as an UNBOUNDED CLASS, generated not enumerated: 21 heads × 10 empty-argument spellings = 210, all ok:false, every failure carrying a css_syntax issue whose caret is in-bounds. MT-F024 asserted EXECUTABLY in the same file: the published parseCssColor THROWS for all 210 (TypeError), and the six guarded heads (var env hsv kelvin ictcp jzazbz) are the only empty forms it survives. Plus 80 hostile inputs (control chars, emoji, Arabic-Indic digits, 100 000-char idents, unbalanced parens, prototype keys), 5000 seeded-mulberry32 fuzz strings (replayable — a fuzz corpus that cannot be replayed is not evidence), and 7 non-string arguments smuggled in from untyped JS. THE TRY/CATCH IS PROVEN NOT LOAD-BEARING: the RAW `colorRoot.parseState` is run over every one of those ~5300 inputs and never throws, and `parseColorNode(x).ok === !raw.isError` for all of them.
  THE ONE HONEST EXCEPTION, PINNED NOT HIDDEN: the var()-fallback / env()-tail / relative-body balanced tail is genuinely recursive, so nesting depth costs JS stack frames. Measured on this build: 2 000 nested parens parse, 3 000 overflow. The guard converts that RangeError into an ordinary ok:false. Test asserts BOTH halves — that the raw graph throws at 20 000 and that the entry point does not.

CSS-L4 CORPUS — 182 tests. 118 positive rows (brief asked ≥40) across hex, named, rgb modern+legacy, hsl, hwb, lab, lch, oklab, oklch, color(), clamping (18 rows), missing components (9 rows), case folding and whitespace. EVERY expected value is written as a spec-derived arithmetic expression — `(50 * 255) / 100`, `0.25 * 360`, `0x80 / 255` — never a decimal literal copied from the parser's output, because a corpus transcribed from the implementation asserts only that the implementation is deterministic. 48-row negative corpus, each row citing the section it violates.
  ONE DECLARED OVER-ACCEPT, pinned by its own test rather than left for a reviewer to find: the relative-colour arm is RECOGNISED, not VALIDATED — `rgb(from red)` (missing all three channels) parses to a relative context node, because validating it means implementing css-color-5 channel expressions, which this prototype scopes out.

EQUIVALENCE — 114 tests, against the PUBLISHED tarball vendored byte-for-byte, sha256 of dist/subpaths/css.js asserted in-test = 8b5381305ea26236326f06a38559247b2089a5be7fa78abe43640d0556320c42. THIS MATTERS AND IS A FINDING: the repository's own dist/subpaths/css.js DIFFERS from the published artifact (rebuild of a dirty tree; 14 of 16 dist files hash-identical, css.js and css.d.ts do not). Every sibling prototype in this workspace (denominator/, cand-s-spec/, cand-b-dispatch/) imports `../../../../../../../src/css/grammar` — i.e. measures against the DIRTY WORKING TREE, not against what 4.0.0 actually ships. cand-O is the only one measuring the published parser.
  GROUND-C's R6 warning taken literally: every agreement assertion compares {space, channels, alpha} FIELD-FOR-FIELD, never just `ok` — an ok-only differential misses R6 entirely. 81 agreement inputs + ALL 148 <named-color>s in both cases (an independent oracle for cand-O's own generated table) + context-colour agreement + rejection agreement.
  DIVERGENCE LEDGER: 22 rows, each asserted in BOTH directions with a spec citation and a verdict — 21 verdict cand-O, 0 verdict published, 1 verdict neither (color-mix, a real css-color-5 gap in BOTH; the incumbent already ships mixColors on ./color and lacks only the syntax, GROUND-A P-028).
  NEW FINDING, EXECUTABLE: three of the 22 are ACCEPTANCE GAPS, not over-accepts — the published parseCssColor CANNOT PARSE `rgba(r,g,b,a)` OR `hsla(h,s%,l%,a)` AT ALL. It rewrites `,`→` ` and then demands exactly three components, so the four-argument legacy form — the most-deployed colour syntax on the web — returns css_syntax. This confirms GROUND-A's P-012/P-015 by measurement against the published artifact, and it is the row a "the regex is fine, it is just lenient" reading cannot absorb. I discovered it because six of my agreement rows failed on first run; I moved them to the ledger rather than deleting them.
  The other 18 cand-O rows: R1/MT-F024 throw · R6 hsl number-as-percentage (50 vs 0.5) · §8.1 clamping · §4.2 alpha clamp (incumbent REJECTS alpha 1.5) · 1e400 absorbed by the clamp · mixed separators · none-in-legacy · heterogeneous legacy triple · trailing comma (P-037) · empty slash (P-037) · percentage <hue> · hwb/oklch comma forms · legacy hsl bare numbers · `1.` as a number · trailing paren · color() alpha clamp · negative chroma clamp.

WHAT I WOULD TELL THE JURY. Correctness: cand-O closes R1 as a class, closes four §8/§9 over-accepts, closes the alpha-clamp rejection, and closes the rgba()/hsla() four-argument GAP — while agreeing bit-for-bit with the incumbent on 81 spot inputs and all 148 named colours. Cost: parity on accepted input, ~1.6× slower on rejected input, one declared over-accept in the relative arm, and one stack-depth limit at ~2 500 nested parens that the guard absorbs. Nothing in that list is hidden in prose; all of it is a test.

result.headline: cand-O wins on measurement — spec-table architecture (eight functions as one production), bit-for-bit drop-in fidelity on every contested divergence (hue unwrapped, xyz-d50 adapted, no Infinity in the AST), 355/355 vs 210/210 re-verified, both GREEN on R1 where published throws 102/172; the two grammars agree on 30,000 fuzz inputs with zero disagreements, and the regex parser is NOT fastest on accepted input on this box (both candidates ~1.2x faster at node level, cand-O drop-in parity) though it IS fastest on the reject path — adoption stands on totality + maintainability, with cand-O owing cand-F labelled failure diagnostics, reject-path budget, and depth-bounded recursion.
result.dissent: Four live disagreements preserved in the apotheosis: (1) token juxtaposition rgb(50%20%30%) — cand-O accepts per css-syntax token-stream reading (browsers agree), cand-F and the published parser reject; adopted cand-O's reading but flagged for owner overrule as it widens acceptance vs the incumbent. (2) Non-finite numerals — three-way split (published rejects 1e400, cand-O clamps-or-fails color_non_finite, cand-F admits Infinity into the AST); sided with cand-O, GROUND-C contract question still deserves an owner ruling. (3) try/catch posture — cand-F's no-shield totality-by-construction is tenable once the wave lands cand-O's balanced tail with an explicit depth bound; recorded as live disagreement, not settled doctrine. (4) Bench epistemics — the prior gate's 'live regex ~1.8x fastest' is not reproduced by three independent measurements, but OC-1 owns the bench bar and nothing here pre-empts it.
